title: Model serving rollout readiness + KPI escalation ladder
summary: Operational checklist and KPI ladder for rolling out new model-serving configurations (quantization + batching changes) to hosted and dedicated customers. Focuses on launch readiness gates, measurable KPIs (latency, token burn rate, cache hit, fallback ratio), and a three-step escalation ladder tied to SLA & cost impact.
scope: Applies to any rollout that changes the inference execution path: kernel changes, quantization profile swaps, batching policy adjustments, or model variant replacements. Excludes purely client-side SDK updates or Console UI-only changes.
readiness_gates:
1) Safety and correctness: unit/integration tests, regen prompt set pass rate >= 98%
2) Performance baseline: canary latency and throughput validated against baseline traffic shape (90th P95 latency delta <= +15% for P50 and P95)
3) Cost & capacity: simulated token burn and GPU slot occupancy modeled for expected peak; < 12% buffer required for autoscale policies
4) Observability: dashboards, alerts, trace sampling, and postmortem templates created
5) Rollback playbook: verified rollback build, DB/metadata compatibility confirmed, canary revert time measured < 15 minutes
kpi_definitions:
Latency tail (P95/P99): end-to-end request latency including routing and model inference. Target: P95 < 1200ms hosted, < 600ms dedicated.
Token burn velocity: tokens/sec consumed at peak normalized per 1K requests. Used to estimate cost acceleration and pre-buy capacity. Alert if observed > 1.5x predicted.
Cache hit rate (prefix + KV): fraction of requests served from warmed cache. Target > 45% within 10 minutes of rollout for steady workloads.
Model fallback ratio: percent of requests routed to fallback variant (e.g., smaller or unquantized model). Target < 2% sustained; >5% triggers rapid review.
Error budget consumption: ratio of 4xx/5xx errors to total requests compared to allowed SLA budget. Alert at >40% burn of weekly budget.
Cold-start ratio: fraction of requests that hit a cold container/GPU allocation causing >2x latency. Target <3% for dedicated pools.
Quality regression (eval set pass): regression flakiness measured on canonical eval set. Threshold: no regression >1% absolute on primary metric (e.g., Rouge/Exact Match).
Operational cost delta: delta in $/1M tokens vs baseline rolling 7d. Flag if +25% or more for hosted tier.
kpi_thresholds_and_actions:
Green: KPIs within targets => continue rollout.
Amber: any KPI in amber (e.g., P95 +15-30%, fallback 2-5%, token burn 1.5x predicted) => pause new region rollouts, execute mitigation checklist (throttle, increase cache warmers, reduce batch size), notify stakeholders.
Red: any KPI in red (P95 > +30%, fallback >5%, error budget >50% consumed) => immediate rollback to previous variant for impacted traffic, cross-team war room, postmortem within 48 hours.
escalation_ladder:
Tier 1 (On-call owner): alert paging for threshold breaches; quick triage (15 minutes) and immediate mitigation (routes, throttles). Owners: serving-runtime on-call + product-ops.
Tier 2 (Response lead): if unresolved after 30 minutes or outage affecting >5% of traffic: convene cross-functional response (runtime eng, infra, SRE, solutions). Action: temporary fallback to baseline model variant, increase autoscale, enable degraded feature gates.
Tier 3 (Executive & Customer Ops): if incident elevates (>1 hour, >20% customers affected, or SLA breach imminent): notify Head of Product Ops + Sales/CS for customer communication and coordinate credits/SLAs. Post-incident review owner assigned within 24 hours.
capacity_burn_tracker_notes:
Use this short tracker during canary and regional ramp: lines in dashboard: date,time,region,requests_per_sec,avg_tokens_per_request,projected_tokens_1h,observed_GPU_occupancy(%),predicted_autoscale_gap(%),notes. Example row: 2025-02-15,14:12,eu-west-1,120rps,320tokens,13.8M,78%,12%gap,KV-cache warming ongoing.
Run the tracker at 5-minute cadence for first 2 hours after any batch/quant change. If occupancy >85% sustained for 10 minutes, pause ramp and execute capacity relief (reduce burst window, increase pool size if available).
canary_plan:
1) Canary cohort size: start with 0.5% of global traffic or up to 5 rps per region (whichever is larger).
2) Canary duration: minimum 60 minutes steady state, but extend to 180 minutes if any amber signals.
3) Monitoring: P95/P99 latency, error rate, cache hit, fallback ratio, token burn velocity.
4) Gradual increments: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with metric validation gates at each step.
5) Abort conditions: any red KPI or repeated auto-reversions from runtime.
6) Canary artifacts needed: canary config, traffic split rules, canary dashboard, ticket with linked timelines.
rollback_criteria:
Immediate rollback triggers: sustained red KPI for 5 minutes, catastrophic error rate (>20% 5xx), customer-reported data corruption.
Planned rollback steps: set traffic to previous variant, instruct autoscaler to adopt baseline profile, clear warm caches to avoid mixed-state, verify smoke tests, reopen incremental ramp after postmortem adjustments.
Rollback owner: serving-runtime engineer on-call (execute), product-ops (coordinate comms), SRE (networking/infra checks).
comms_plan:
Internal: Slack #prodops-runbook pings at each canary milestone. War room bridge for Tier 2 incidents.
External: CS/customer-notice templated message if >5% customers impacted. Include ETA, mitigation steps, and contact.
Postmortem: initial incident note within 12 hours, full written postmortem within 72 hours. Share to confluence and tag affected sales/account owners.
